```{r setup, include=FALSE}
figure_dir <- params$figure_dir
if(is.null(figure_dir)) {figure_dir <- tempfile("traffic-figures-");dir.create(figure_dir)}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE,
  fig.path=file.path(figure_dir,"figure-"), dev="png", dpi=150,
  fig.width=10, fig.height=8, out.width="100%", cache=FALSE)
fmt <- function(v,digits=2) format(round(v,digits),trim=TRUE,scientific=FALSE,big.mark=",")
stopifnot(is.logical(params$export),length(params$export)==1L,!is.na(params$export))
```

## Sources and measurements

The case covers 24 hourly frames on 2026-06-16. Los Angeles Area contains
D07/D08/D12 links; San Francisco Bay Area contains D04 links. Each region has a
separate map, coverage table, flow trend and CHP start-count trend below.

The cache holds 98,688 Los Angeles active-position hourly values from
`flow_2026_06.binz`, 659,808 D04 five-minute source-station counts from
`d04_text_station_5min_2026_06_16.txt.gz`, and 1,023 district-day CHP summaries.
Available positions are averaged within Los Angeles stations. The D04 metadata join retains 658,944 values at 2,288 stations. D04 requires all
twelve five-minute counts per station-hour before summation. Links use the mean
of available endpoint station values, in vehicles/hour. Shared station values
make link sums unsuitable as regional counts of distinct vehicles.

CHP records retain reported source-clock timestamps and locations. Categories
use the supplied source-type lookup; curated source descriptions are retained.
District and geographic filters retain 1,019 starts: 700 in Los Angeles and 319
in D04. Four Los Angeles district-day records lie outside the supplied extent.
Verified end times are unavailable, so an event marker represents a reported
start in one hour, not its duration or a verified effect on flow.

## Data preparation

`data/source.rds` contains the selected source-level records and supplied geometry.
`prepare.R` converts them to the common input without downloading data. Its
executed implementation appears in Appendix A. The generated `data/input.rds` is
then read by the common package.

```{r prepare}
library(bdynets)
source("prepare.R")
prepared_file <- prepare_example(".")
x <- read_traffic(prepared_file)
input <- readRDS(prepared_file)
index <- match(params$time_label,sub("^.* ","",x$time_labels))
stopifnot(!is.na(index))
```

The map starts at `r x$time_labels[index]` and covers
`r x$interval_seconds[index]/60` minutes. The default 08:00 is a demonstration
selection, not a maximum-based selection. Numeric seconds and displayed labels
retain the supplied source clock; they do not establish a UTC offset.

```{r scope}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Region=x$regions,
  Roads=vapply(x$regions,function(z)sum(x$roads$region==z),integer(1)),
  Whole_day_starts=vapply(x$regions,function(z)sum(x$events$region==z),integer(1))),
  caption="Whole-day regional scope")
knitr::kable(head(input$flow),caption="Actual prepared road-hour records")
knitr::kable(head(input$events[c("id","time_label","lon","lat","category","region")]),
  caption="Actual prepared event records")
```

| Common field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| road_id, geometry | Unique display link and travel-ordered longitude/latitude vertices |
| from_station, to_station | Endpoint source station identifiers |
| time, flow | Source-clock hour start and endpoint-mean hourly rate |
| id, time, lon, lat | Unique report ID, reported start and coordinates |
| category, description | Source-type classification and retained source text |
| region | Explicit geographic selection label |

Both regions use the same object, plot method and global log1p thresholds.
Their central-area views do not restrict regional statistics. Red diamonds mark
starts in the selected hour. Geographic overlap alone does not establish a
relationship between a report and a road measurement.

## Los Angeles Area

```{r la-map, fig.cap="Los Angeles Area: road flow and CHP reported starts in the selected hour. Colors use the same full-day, two-region thresholds."}
region <- "Los Angeles Area"
plot(x,index=index,region=region)
```

```{r la-statistics}
cols <- which(x$roads$region==region)
v <- x$values[,cols,drop=FALSE]
events <- x$events[x$events$region==region,,drop=FALSE]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Statistic=c("Roads","Road-hour cells","Observed cells","Missing cells","Zero cells","Whole-day starts"),
  Value=c(ncol(v),length(v),sum(!is.na(v)),sum(is.na(v)),sum(v==0,na.rm=TRUE),nrow(events))),
  caption="Whole-day coverage")
selected <- traffic_summary(x,index=index,region=region)
knitr::kable(selected[c("time","available","missing","zero","events")],
  caption="Selected-hour observations and starts")
knitr::kable(selected[c("minimum","median","mean","p95","maximum")],
  digits=2,caption="Selected-hour distribution [vehicles/hour]")
```

At `r selected$time`, mean available-link flow is `r fmt(selected$mean)`
vehicles/hour, with `r selected$events` reported starts in this hour.
The whole-day total is `r nrow(events)` starts. These statistics have different
time scopes. The 56 unavailable links in each hour produce 1,344 missing road-hour cells. The hourly export does not establish complete five-minute coverage for every underlying Los Angeles station.

```{r la-flow-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Regional mean available-link flow by hour. The dashed line marks the selected map hour."}
trend <- traffic_trend(x,region=region)
plot(trend$time,trend$mean,type="l",lwd=2,col="#365c70",xaxt="n",
     xlab="Source time",ylab="Mean link flow [vehicles/hour]")
at <- c(1,5,9,13,17,21,24)
axis(1,at=trend$time[at],labels=sub("^.* ","",trend$label[at]))
abline(v=x$times[index],lty=2,col="#7b858b")
flow_peak <- which.max(trend$mean)
```

The greatest regional mean is `r fmt(trend$mean[flow_peak])` vehicles/hour at
`r trend$label[flow_peak]`. Missing link values are excluded from the mean.
This curve does not measure speed or regional vehicle totals.

```{r la-event-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Reported event starts per source-clock hour, without inferred durations."}
plot(trend$time,trend$events,type="h",lwd=5,col="#9b4840",xaxt="n",
     xlab="Source time",ylab="Reported starts")
axis(1,at=trend$time[at],labels=sub("^.* ","",trend$label[at]))
event_peak <- which.max(trend$events)
```

The largest hourly count is `r trend$events[event_peak]` starts at
`r trend$label[event_peak]`. A coincident change in flow would not by itself
establish an event effect.

## San Francisco Bay Area

```{r bay-map, fig.cap="San Francisco Bay Area: road flow and CHP reported starts in the selected hour. Colors use the same full-day, two-region thresholds."}
region <- "San Francisco Bay Area"
plot(x,index=index,region=region)
```

```{r bay-statistics}
cols <- which(x$roads$region==region)
v <- x$values[,cols,drop=FALSE]
events <- x$events[x$events$region==region,,drop=FALSE]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Statistic=c("Roads","Road-hour cells","Observed cells","Missing cells","Zero cells","Whole-day starts"),
  Value=c(ncol(v),length(v),sum(!is.na(v)),sum(is.na(v)),sum(v==0,na.rm=TRUE),nrow(events))),
  caption="Whole-day coverage")
selected <- traffic_summary(x,index=index,region=region)
knitr::kable(selected[c("time","available","missing","zero","events")],
  caption="Selected-hour observations and starts")
knitr::kable(selected[c("minimum","median","mean","p95","maximum")],
  digits=2,caption="Selected-hour distribution [vehicles/hour]")
```

At `r selected$time`, mean available-link flow is `r fmt(selected$mean)`
vehicles/hour, with `r selected$events` reported starts in this hour.
The whole-day total is `r nrow(events)` starts. These statistics have different
time scopes. All 52,872 D04 road-hour values are present. The source has 2,291 mainline stations; 400665, 406767 and 418817 lack matched geometry and are excluded. The 2,288 retained stations have complete five-minute timestamps. Detector imputation may still be present. Six event summaries lack detail messages and remain included.

```{r bay-flow-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Regional mean available-link flow by hour. The dashed line marks the selected map hour."}
trend <- traffic_trend(x,region=region)
plot(trend$time,trend$mean,type="l",lwd=2,col="#365c70",xaxt="n",
     xlab="Source time",ylab="Mean link flow [vehicles/hour]")
at <- c(1,5,9,13,17,21,24)
axis(1,at=trend$time[at],labels=sub("^.* ","",trend$label[at]))
abline(v=x$times[index],lty=2,col="#7b858b")
flow_peak <- which.max(trend$mean)
```

The greatest regional mean is `r fmt(trend$mean[flow_peak])` vehicles/hour at
`r trend$label[flow_peak]`. Missing link values are excluded from the mean.
This curve does not measure speed or regional vehicle totals.

```{r bay-event-trend, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Reported event starts per source-clock hour, without inferred durations."}
plot(trend$time,trend$events,type="h",lwd=5,col="#9b4840",xaxt="n",
     xlab="Source time",ylab="Reported starts")
axis(1,at=trend$time[at],labels=sub("^.* ","",trend$label[at]))
event_peak <- which.max(trend$events)
```

The largest hourly count is `r trend$events[event_peak]` starts at
`r trend$label[event_peak]`. A coincident change in flow would not by itself
establish an event effect.

## Figure and data export

Both regional exports call the same package interface. They contain PNG/PDF
maps and trends, exact selected records, summary/trend CSV files, metadata,
input/output MD5 checksums and runtime information. The selection retains the
complete input's scale; it is an inspection artifact, not a new input bundle.
Existing export directories are refused. The report parameter `export` defaults
to false and creates no export directory during ordinary rendering.

```{r export}
if(params$export) {
  label <- gsub("[^[:alnum:]_-]+","-",x$time_labels[index])
  for(region in x$regions) {
    name <- gsub(" ","-",tolower(region))
    traffic_export(x,file.path(params$export_dir,paste(name,label,sep="-")),
      index=index,region=region,
      input_files=c(source="data/source.rds",prepared="data/input.rds"))
  }
}
```

## Basemap source

The figures use the supplied offline OSM-derived context. Basemap build dates
identify the context snapshot, independently of the traffic date or simulation
day. Generalized map features are suitable for display, not a routable road graph.
Map data © [OpenStreetMap contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright);
basemap extraction uses Protomaps archives distributed as ODbL Produced Works.

```{r basemap-source, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
p <- input$provenance$basemap
extracts <- if(is.null(p$extracts)) list(list(region="Supplied context",provenance=p)) else p$extracts
for(e in extracts) {
  q <- e$provenance
  bounds <- paste(format(unlist(q$bbox_south_west_north_east),digits=7,trim=TRUE),collapse=", ")
  tab <- data.frame(Item=c("Region","Archive URL","Build date","Retrieved UTC","Zoom","Recorded bounds (south, west, north, east)","License"),
    Value=c(e$region,q$source_url,q$build_date,q$retrieved_utc,q$zoom,bounds,q$license))
  cat(knitr::kable(tab,format="html"),"\n\n")
}
```

The source cache preserves the original tile records and geometry checksums.
The cache MD5 below identifies the actual bundled copy used for this report.

The two extracts provide separate regional context. Their bounding envelope
does not imply continuous cached coverage between the regions. Both basemap
snapshots postdate the traffic day and do not reconstruct its historical roads.

## Appendix A: preparation implementation

The following code is the source-to-input transformation executed from
`prepare.R`. The input cache supplies all objects used by this function.

```{r preparation-source, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("```r\n",paste(readLines("prepare.R"),collapse="\n"),"\n```\n",sep="")
```

## Appendix B: verification and runtime

```{r verification}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Check=names(input$provenance$preparation_check),
  Value=unlist(input$provenance$preparation_check)),caption="Executed preparation checks")
knitr::kable(data.frame(File=c("source.rds","input.rds"),
  Bytes=unname(file.info(c("data/source.rds","data/input.rds"))$size),
  MD5=unname(tools::md5sum(c("data/source.rds","data/input.rds")))),
  caption="Actual bundled files")
sessionInfo()
```
